newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary opens talks with investors on energy hikes.
newsitem.headline: Hungary opens talks with investors on energy hikes.

text.p: Talks started on Tuesday with the foreign investors in the Hungarian energy sector on energy price increases due on January 1.

The talks, held in the Hungarian Energy Office (MEH) were attended by MEH experts, government commissioner responsible energy prices Imre Karl, and representatives of shareholders in the gas sector, Hungarian news agency MTI reported.

Karl, who was appointed by the government in September after it rejected the MEH's proposal for a reported 40 percent energy price increase for October, said he would sound out investors' opinions before recommending a new year energy price to the government by the end of October.
"The review has reached the stage where it is possible and justified to hold coordination talks with Hungarian and foreign investors in the sector," Karl told MTI.
Tuesday's talks were held with gas suppliers. Electricity suppliers will join on Wednesday while other companies involved in the sector will be contacted later, Karl said.

The talks, which Karl said would be complete within two weeks, were promised by former Minister for Trade and Industry Tamas Suchman, who was sacked on Sunday following a corruption scandal within the state privatisation agency APV.

The decision to delay the rises until January dismayed western utilities from Germany, France, Belgium and Italy who invested more than $2 billion dollars in the energy sector in a wave of privatisations completed at the end of last year.
They had been assured of an eight percent return on investment from 1997, a move which was to have involved a price adjustment in October.
